entries.title: Lesion Localization (CNS vs. PNS Localization Framework)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 117's key objective directly requires the candidate to 'characterize the distribution and/or localize the lesion' when assessing weakness; this unit teaches the CNS-vs-PNS and cortical/subcortical/brainstem/spinal-cord/PNS localization framework that is the mechanical basis of that competency, applied throughout the chapter's focal-deficit units.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 66's enabling objectives require history/exam findings aimed at determining the 'distribution of symptoms'; this unit's localization framework underlies that distribution-based reasoning for numbness/altered sensation.

testable_competencies.localization: Given a described pattern of motor, sensory, or reflex findings, classify the lesion as cortical, subcortical, brainstem, cerebellar, spinal cord, anterior horn cell, nerve root, or peripheral nerve/NMJ/muscle, and state the localizing implication (e.g., crossed findings = brainstem; sensory level = cord).

entries.title: Neurological Examination (Mental Status, Cranial Nerve, Motor, Sensory, Coordination/Gait)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This unit's motor/sensory/coordination exam technique is the physical-examination sub-skill explicitly required by objective 117's enabling objectives ('results of an appropriate history and physical examination').

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The Mental Status Exam component is the physical-examination sub-skill named in objective 58-3's enabling objectives ('the determination of the patient's mental status as well as the Mini-Mental State Examination').

testable_competencies.exam_technique: Perform and correctly interpret each component of the bedside neurological exam (mental status, CN I-XII, tone/power/reflexes, primary sensory modalities, coordination and gait) as the shared physical-exam substrate for every focal-deficit presentation in this chapter.

entries.title: Neuroanatomy Review

testable_competencies.foundational: Background neuroanatomy (pathways, vascular territories) supporting localization and stroke-syndrome competencies tested in later units; not independently testable.

entries.zero_question_reason: Foundational anatomy/physiology background, not independently testable at the MCCQE level; frames the localization, stroke-syndrome, and cranial-nerve competencies tested in later units.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 39's (Headache) enabling objectives explicitly require the candidate to know 'indications and contraindications for lumbar puncture'.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 58-1's (Coma) enabling objectives list lumbar puncture among the critical investigations for coma.

testable_competencies.procedure: State indications, contraindications, and interpretation basics of lumbar puncture (opening pressure, CSF analysis) as used in the headache, coma, and CNS-infection diagnostic pathways.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This unit's title and content directly match objective 117's full presentation scope: differentiating true weakness from fatigue/pain, localizing to muscle/nerve/UMN, and determining cause.

testable_competencies.approach: Given a patient with weakness, differentiate true weakness from fatigue/pain/inhibition, localize to muscle/peripheral nerve/UMN pathway, and determine the most likely underlying cause and initial workup.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This unit's title and content directly match objective 66's full presentation scope (numbness/tingling/altered sensation): history, exam, targeted investigation, and initial management.

testable_competencies.approach: Given a patient with numbness/tingling, take a history and perform an exam aimed at the underlying cause (e.g., diabetic, compressive, demyelinating) and construct an initial management/referral plan.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This unit's title and content directly match objective 35's full presentation scope (ataxia/gait disturbance): distinguishing ataxia from other gait irregularities and localizing/determining cause.

testable_competencies.approach: Given a patient with a gait disturbance, differentiate ataxic from other gait patterns (e.g., spastic, parkinsonian, steppage), localize the level of the nervous system involved, and determine cause.

entries.title: Cranial Nerve Deficits (CN I-XII Localizing Syndromes)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: CN III/IV/VI palsies are the leading cause category for objective 23 (Diplopia); this unit's oculomotor/trochlear/abducens content is a component of that objective's differential.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: CN VIII (vestibulocochlear) content is a component of objective 40 (Hearing loss)'s differential for sensorineural hearing loss.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: CN VII (facial nerve) palsy is a component of objective 117 (Weakness)'s localization framework applied to the face.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Isolated cranial mononeuropathies are a component of objective 109-11 (Nerve injury)'s broader peripheral/cranial nerve injury scope, though 109-11 is framed around traumatic nerve injury rather than the medical causes emphasized here.

testable_competencies.localization: Given a described deficit pattern (e.g., ptosis with a 'down and out' eye, facial droop sparing the forehead, hoarseness with dysphagia), identify the cranial nerve involved and the most likely level/cause of the lesion.

entries.title: Neuro-Ophthalmology (Optic Neuropathy, Atrophy, Disc Edema, Visual Field Defects, Amaurosis Fugax, Pupil Abnormalities)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Optic neuropathy, disc edema, and amaurosis fugax are acute-onset causes of visual disturbance directly within objective 115-1's scope (acute visual disturbance/loss).

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Cerebrovascular accident and transient ischemic attack (stroke)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Amaurosis fugax is explicitly named as an example finding in objective 41's (stroke/TIA) key objective ('acute neurological deficits (e.g., aphasia, amaurosis fugax)').

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Given visual symptoms/findings (painless vision loss, disc pallor vs. edema, a specific visual field defect pattern, transient monocular vision loss, or an abnormal pupillary light response), identify the likely neuro-ophthalmologic diagnosis and localize the lesion along the visual pathway.

entries.title: Eye Movement Disorders (Internuclear Ophthalmoplegia, Diplopia, Nystagmus)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Diplopia is this unit's own titled subheading and directly matches objective 23's full scope.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Given diplopia, nystagmus, or a specific eye-movement abnormality (e.g., failure of adduction on lateral gaze), determine whether it is monocular or binocular, localize the lesion (e.g., MLF for INO), and identify the likely cause.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: B12/nutritional and toxic peripheral neuropathies are a component cause within objective 66's (numbness/altered sensation) differential.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Alcohol/toxin-related neurologic injury overlaps with objective 103's (substance use disorders) scope, though 103 is framed around the addiction/substance-use encounter rather than the resulting neurologic deficit itself.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize the clinical patterns of common nutritional (e.g., B12, thiamine) and toxic (e.g., alcohol, heavy metal) neurologic injuries and their reversibility with treatment.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This unit's content directly matches objective 92's full scope, including its explicit requirement to 'outline a plan for the emergent treatment of a patient presenting with a seizure' (i.e., status epilepticus).

testable_competencies.management: Given a patient with a seizure, differentiate seizure from non-seizure mimics, classify seizure type, identify triggers/underlying causes, and manage both routine and emergent (status epilepticus) presentations, including counselling on driving restrictions.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This unit's title and content directly match objective 58-2's full scope.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize delirium (acute onset, fluctuating course, altered level of consciousness/attention), differentiate it from dementia and psychiatric disorders, identify the underlying cause, and initiate urgent management.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: MCI is the early/mild end of objective 58-3's spectrum ('major or mild neurocognitive disorders'); the objective's title explicitly includes the mild form.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize MCI as cognitive decline with preserved independence in activities of daily living, and identify it as a risk state for progression to major neurocognitive disorder.

entries.title: Major Neurocognitive Disorder / Dementia (Overview, Alzheimer's, Lewy Body, Frontotemporal, and Vascular Subtypes)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This unit's content directly matches objective 58-3's full scope, including its explicit instruction to 'differentiate early Alzheimer disease from other causes' - i.e., distinguish Alzheimer's from Lewy Body, frontotemporal, and vascular dementia.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Given a patient with progressive cognitive decline, distinguish dementia from delirium/depression, and differentiate Alzheimer's, Lewy body, frontotemporal, and vascular dementia by their distinguishing clinical features (e.g., early visual hallucinations/parkinsonism in DLB, early personality/behavioural change in FTD, stepwise decline in vascular dementia), and screen for reversible causes.

entries.title: Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: CJD is a rare, rapidly progressive cause within objective 58-3's broad dementia differential; the objective's key/enabling text does not name CJD specifically.

testable_competencies.red_flag: Recognize rapidly progressive dementia (weeks-months) with myoclonus as a red flag for CJD, distinguishing tempo from the typical slow-progressive dementias.

entries.zero_question_reason: Rare prion disease; graduating-student-level competency is limited to recognizing the rapid-tempo red flag rather than independently testable diagnostic/management detail.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Aphasia is a language disorder directly within objective 44's (Language and speech disorders) scope.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Cerebrovascular accident and transient ischemic attack (stroke)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Aphasia is explicitly named as an example finding in objective 41's (stroke/TIA) key objective ('acute neurological deficits (e.g., aphasia, amaurosis fugax)').

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Given a patient with a language deficit, distinguish aphasia (language) from dysarthria (speech), classify by fluency/comprehension/repetition (e.g., Broca's vs. Wernicke's), and localize to the dominant hemisphere.

entries.title: Apraxia and Agnosia

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Cerebrovascular accident and transient ischemic attack (stroke)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Apraxia/agnosia can occur as non-dominant/dominant hemisphere cortical stroke findings within objective 41's broader neurologic-deficit scope, but neither is independently named in objective 41's key/enabling text.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize apraxia (inability to perform learned motor tasks despite intact strength/sensation) and agnosia (inability to recognize stimuli despite intact primary sensory function) as cortical higher-function deficits distinct from primary motor/sensory loss.

entries.zero_question_reason: Thin content with no dedicated MCC objective; graduating-student-level competency is limited to recognizing these as cortical (not primary motor/sensory) deficits, tested if at all as a minor component of the stroke/dementia units.
entries.mcc_evidence_retention_reason: WEAK evidence retained (rather than cleared to []) because apraxia/agnosia are genuine, named cortical-localization findings relevant to the stroke and dementia units' differential reasoning, even though neither has independently sufficient MCC evidence for a stronger classification.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This unit's title and content directly match objective 109-10's scope (traumatic brain injury): diagnosis, severity assessment, and management including imaging and surveillance.

testable_competencies.management: Given a patient with mild TBI/concussion, determine need for imaging/observation vs. hospitalization, counsel on post-concussive sequelae and return-to-play, and recognize red flags for repeat injury.

entries.title: Neuro-Oncology: Paraneoplastic Syndromes and Tumours of the Nervous System

testable_competencies.awareness: Recognize that paraneoplastic neurologic syndromes and CNS tumours are addressed in full in the Endocrinology and Neurosurgery chapters respectively; this chapter contributes no independent content.

entries.zero_question_reason: Both subsections are pure cross-references to other chapters (Endocrinology E56, Neurosurgery NS12) with zero independent body content in the Neurology chapter.
entries.cross_discipline_note: Primary content ownership: Neurosurgery (Tumours of the Nervous System) and Endocrinology (Paraneoplastic Syndromes). This unit exists only to preserve source-node traceability for the TN heading; substantive coverage should be scoped under those chapters, not duplicated here.

entries.title: Movement Disorders: Basal Ganglia Physiology

testable_competencies.foundational: Basal ganglia direct/indirect pathway physiology as background for the movement-disorder units.

entries.zero_question_reason: Foundational physiology background, not independently testable; frames the Parkinson's/Huntington's/other movement-disorder units.

entries.title: Signs and Symptoms of Movement Disorders

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 61's key objective requires 'careful observation...to describe the abnormal movement accurately and differentiate between the types and causes of movement disorders' - this unit's semiology content is that observational skill.

testable_competencies.semiology: Classify an observed abnormal movement as hyperkinetic (tremor, chorea, dystonia, tics, myoclonus) or hypokinetic (bradykinesia, rigidity) and describe it accurately.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 61's enabling objectives explicitly require 'identification of key physical findings characteristic of Parkinson disease (e.g., rigidity, akinesia)' - Parkinson's disease is the named prototype of this objective.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize the cardinal features of Parkinson's disease (bradykinesia, rigidity, resting tremor, postural instability), differentiate from other parkinsonian syndromes, and outline the initial management approach.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Atypical parkinsonian syndromes are a component of objective 61's differential once Parkinson's disease has been considered and red flags for an atypical course are present.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize red flags (early falls, poor levodopa response, early autonomic failure/dementia) that suggest an atypical parkinsonian syndrome rather than idiopathic Parkinson's disease.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Huntington's disease (chorea) is a component example within objective 61's hyperkinetic movement-disorder differential.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize chorea with autosomal dominant family history and psychiatric/cognitive decline as suggestive of Huntington's disease, and understand the basis for genetic counselling/testing.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Wilson disease is explicitly named in objective 61's enabling objectives as a reversible cause to screen for ('a history and physical examination to look for reversible causes (e.g., medications, Wilson disease)').

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize Wilson's disease (young patient with movement disorder/dystonia plus liver disease/Kayser-Fleischer rings) as a treatable, reversible cause of a movement disorder warranting screening (ceruloplasmin, copper studies).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 61's title explicitly includes 'tic disorders' as a named movement-disorder category.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Classify a tic disorder by motor/vocal tic type and duration criteria (provisional vs. persistent vs. Tourette's), screen for common psychiatric comorbidities (OCD, ADHD), and outline a stepped treatment approach.

entries.title: Cerebellar Disorders: Wernicke-Korsakoff Syndrome and Cerebellar Ataxias

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Cerebellar ataxia is a direct example within objective 35's (ataxia/gait) full scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome is a thiamine-deficiency complication of alcohol use disorder, overlapping objective 103's (substance use disorders) scope for identifying and managing alcohol-related medical complications.

testable_competencies.emergency_recognition: Recognize Wernicke encephalopathy (confusion, ataxia, ophthalmoplegia) as a reversible medical emergency requiring emergent thiamine before glucose, and distinguish cerebellar (truncal/limb) ataxia from sensory ataxia on exam.

entries.title: Vertigo

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This heading's title and the referenced Otolaryngology chapter content directly match objective 24's full scope (dizziness and vertigo, including central-vs-peripheral differentiation).

testable_competencies.differentiation: Differentiate central from peripheral vertigo using history and bedside exam (e.g., HINTS), recognizing which presentations require urgent neurologic vs. ENT workup.

entries.cross_discipline_note: This heading is a cross-reference-only entry in the Neurology chapter ('see Otolaryngology, OT12'); primary content ownership and detailed coverage belong to the Otolaryngology chapter. Retained here at low weight because central-vertigo recognition (this chapter's differential responsibility) is directly relevant to objective 24.

entries.title: Motor Neuron Disease: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: ALS is a classic combined UMN+LMN cause of weakness directly within objective 117's diagnostic scope, including the EMG/NCS investigations explicitly named in 117's enabling objectives.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize combined upper and lower motor neuron signs without sensory involvement as characteristic of ALS, outline the EMG/NCS and imaging workup used to support the diagnosis, and describe disease-modifying (riluzole) vs. supportive management.

entries.title: Other Motor Neuron Diseases

testable_competencies.awareness: Awareness that ALS-variant motor neuron diseases (PLS, PMA, SBMA) exist as a differential once ALS itself has been considered.

entries.zero_question_reason: Rare ALS-variant motor neuron diseases beyond the graduating-student scope; ALS itself (this section's prototype, covered in its own unit) is the testable representative of this category.

entries.title: Peripheral Neuropathies: Classification and Guillain-Barré Syndrome

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: GBS is a classic acute ascending weakness directly within objective 117's diagnostic scope, an emergent LMN-pattern cause requiring urgent recognition (respiratory/autonomic monitoring).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The peripheral-neuropathy classification framework (axonal vs. demyelinating, mononeuropathy vs. polyneuropathy) overlaps objective 109-11's (nerve injury) localization approach, though 109-11 is framed around traumatic rather than medical nerve injury.

testable_competencies.emergency_recognition: Recognize acute ascending, symmetric weakness with areflexia (± antecedent infection) as GBS, initiate urgent monitoring for respiratory/autonomic failure, and classify peripheral neuropathies by distribution and fibre type (axonal vs. demyelinating).

entries.title: Neuromuscular Junction Disorders: Myasthenia Gravis, Lambert-Eaton Myasthenic Syndrome, and Botulism

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: NMJ disorders are a classic muscle/NMJ-source cause of weakness directly within objective 117's diagnostic scope, distinguished by the fatigability pattern the objective's history-taking is aimed at eliciting.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Differentiate myasthenia gravis (fatigable weakness, worsens with activity, ocular/bulbar onset), Lambert-Eaton (proximal weakness that improves with repeated activity, paraneoplastic association), and botulism (descending paralysis, autonomic findings) by pattern and outline the initial workup (e.g., antibody testing, EMG) for each.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Myopathies are the 'muscle' source category within objective 117's localization framework (muscle vs. peripheral nerve vs. UMN).

testable_competencies.classification: Classify a myopathy by etiologic category (inflammatory, endocrine, toxic, infectious, hereditary dystrophy/metabolic/periodic-paralysis/mitochondrial) using the pattern of proximal vs. distal weakness and key investigations (CK, biopsy).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Myotonic dystrophy is a named hereditary-dystrophy example within objective 117's muscle-source differential.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize the characteristic distal-greater-than-proximal weakness, myotonia (delayed muscle relaxation), frontal balding, and cardiac conduction abnormalities of myotonic dystrophy type 1, and its autosomal dominant trinucleotide-repeat inheritance with anticipation.

entries.title: Pain Syndromes: Neuropathic Pain, Trigeminal Neuralgia, Postherpetic Neuralgia, Painful Diabetic Neuropathy, and Complex Regional Pain Syndrome

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This unit's overarching topic and every named sub-syndrome are direct examples within objective 67-2-2's (central/peripheral neuropathic pain) full scope.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize the clinical pattern of neuropathic pain (burning, shooting, allodynia) and identify the specific syndrome (trigeminal neuralgia, postherpetic neuralgia, painful diabetic neuropathy, CRPS) from history, then outline first-line pharmacotherapy.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This unit's content directly matches objective 39's full scope, including its explicit instruction to differentiate benign (e.g., migraine) from serious causes of headache.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Differentiate primary headache disorders (migraine, tension, cluster) from secondary causes using red-flag features, apply migraine diagnostic criteria, and outline abortive/prophylactic management while avoiding medication-overuse headache.

entries.title: Sleep Disorders (Overview, Insomnia, Sleep Apnea, Restless Legs Syndrome, Periodic Limb Movement Disorder, Narcolepsy, Parasomnias)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This unit's content directly matches objective 98's full scope (sleep-wake disorders).

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Take a sleep history to differentiate insomnia, sleep apnea, RLS/PLMD, narcolepsy, and parasomnias, screen for safety concerns (e.g., excessive daytime somnolence and driving), and determine when polysomnography or specialized referral is required.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This unit's title and content directly match objective 58-1's full scope.

testable_competencies.emergency_management: Given a comatose patient, assess level of consciousness (e.g., GCS), secure airway/breathing/circulation, pursue an efficient cause-directed workup (glucose, toxin screen, imaging), and initiate empiric emergent treatment (e.g., naloxone, glucose, thiamine).

entries.title: Stroke: Terminology, Pathophysiology, and Vascular Territory Syndromes

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Cerebrovascular accident and transient ischemic attack (stroke)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This unit's content directly matches objective 41's core definitional/pathophysiologic scope and causal-conditions list (ischemic: large vessel/small vessel/cardioembolic; hemorrhagic).

entries.title: Stroke: Assessment and Treatment of Acute Ischemic Stroke

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Cerebrovascular accident and transient ischemic attack (stroke)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This unit's content directly matches objective 41's enabling objectives for acute management, including imaging (CT) and acute medical/surgical intervention.

testable_competencies.management: Given a patient with acute ischemic stroke, apply time-window-based eligibility criteria for IV thrombolysis and endovascular thrombectomy, and initiate acute supportive management (e.g., blood pressure targets).

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Cerebrovascular accident and transient ischemic attack (stroke)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 41's key objective explicitly states the candidate 'will recognize the need for preventive health care in order to decrease the risk of TIA or CVA' - this unit's risk-factor-modification content (hypercholesterolemia, diabetes, smoking, physical activity) directly matches that instruction.

testable_competencies.prevention: Counsel on modifiable stroke risk factors (lipids, glycemic control, smoking cessation, physical activity, antihypertensive/antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapy as indicated) for primary and secondary stroke prevention.

entries.title: Intracranial Hemorrhage

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Cerebrovascular accident and transient ischemic attack (stroke)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 41's causal-conditions list explicitly includes 'Hemorrhage - Intracerebral and cerebellar / Subarachnoid'; this unit's ICH content directly matches that scope.

testable_competencies.management: Given a patient with intracranial hemorrhage, identify the likely etiology (hypertensive, amyloid angiopathy, trauma, AVM/aneurysm), order appropriate investigations, and outline acute blood-pressure and ICP management, recognizing surgical indications requiring Neurosurgery referral.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Surgical/ICP-lowering management detail is cross-referenced in TN to the Neurosurgery chapter (NS8); this unit covers the medical diagnostic/initial-management scope owned by Neurology.

entries.title: Neurocutaneous Syndromes

testable_competencies.awareness: Recognize that neurocutaneous syndromes (e.g., neurofibromatosis, tuberous sclerosis) are addressed in full in the Pediatrics chapter; this chapter contributes no independent content.

entries.zero_question_reason: Pure cross-reference to Pediatrics (P89) with zero independent body content in the Neurology chapter.
entries.cross_discipline_note: Primary content ownership: Pediatrics chapter (P89). This unit exists only to preserve source-node traceability for the TN heading.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Optic neuritis (acute vision loss) is a classic MS presentation directly within objective 115-1's diagnostic scope.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Cerebellar/sensory ataxia is a classic MS presentation directly within objective 35's diagnostic scope.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize MS as episodic, anatomically-disseminated CNS demyelination (e.g., optic neuritis, sensory symptoms, ataxia) in a young adult, describe the relapsing-remitting vs. progressive clinical patterns, and outline the role of MRI/CSF in diagnosis and of disease-modifying therapy.

entries.title: Common Medications (Neurology Reference Table)

testable_competencies.reference: Reference table of common neurologic medications (e.g., antiseizure medications, dopaminergic agents) cross-linking drug class to the disease-specific units where each is discussed.

entries.zero_question_reason: Reference/summary medication table; testable prescribing knowledge is captured within each disease-specific study unit (e.g., seizure, Parkinson's disease) rather than as an independent topic.

entries.title: Landmark Neurology Trials

testable_competencies.awareness: Awareness that management recommendations elsewhere in the Stroke units (e.g., thrombolysis time windows, anticoagulant choice in AFib) are evidence-based, without needing to recall individual trial names/statistics.

do_not_test: Specific trial names, publication years, or numeric outcome statistics (e.g., NNT, hazard ratios) from the landmark-trials table.
entries.zero_question_reason: Individual clinical-trial minutiae (trial names, exact statistics) are specialist-level detail out of scope for a graduating medical student per project accuracy rules; the underlying management conclusions are already captured as testable competencies within the corresponding Stroke study units.
